title: Density, Viscosity, Conductance, and Transference Number of Concentrated Aqueous Magnesium Chloride at 25 C
needs_pass2_reason: text layer needed corrections after the image check (subscript digits misread, comma decimals, O/0, I/1); journal scan
experimental_method: density (details referenced to earlier work; concentrations by gravimetric AgCl analysis), capillary viscometer with electronic stopwatch (relative viscosity), conductance cell, emf of Ag/AgCl concentration cells with and without transference at 298.15 K
uncertainties_stated: duplicate analyses agree to 0.02 % (density and conductance part) and about 0.05 % (others); no explicit uncertainty for density or viscosity
quality_remarks: Authors note their densities for concentrated solutions are slightly higher than Dunn and Perron et al., and consistently larger than Wirth and Bangert.
Table I printed temperature as 298.15 deg K (sic); treated as 298.15 K.
Densities exist for only 20 compositions of the 28 rows; the other rows are conductance-only.

not_extracted_tables.reason: transference numbers of Mg ion constituent (derived by differentiation of a fitted polynomial; not in scope)

extraction_notes: Tables written by script from values transcribed against the page images. Parenthesised literature phi_v values (Wirth and Bangert) split into their own column. Sanity: density increases monotonically with m; relative viscosity monotonic.
